title: Rewrite the 2D skeleton modifier and IK system
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #

This PR rewrites the 2D skeleton modification system to use a node-based modifier architecture similar to the current 3D skeleton modifier system.

The old 2D skeleton system was built around `SkeletonModificationStack2D` and `SkeletonModification2D` resources. In practice, this architecture has been very fragile:

- `SkeletonModificationStack2D` could keep stale references to a `Skeleton2D` after the skeleton was freed or scenes were reloaded.
- Fixing one lifetime issue could expose other problems around deferred cleanup, scene tree state, and physics processing.
- With multi-threaded physics enabled, some failure paths could repeatedly hit error reporting from the physics thread, causing log mutex contention and in some cases freezing the main thread.
- IK and physical bone modifications directly interacted with `Bone2D` node transforms, making runtime pose ownership unclear and easy to desynchronize.
- The old stack/resource model made it difficult to reason about modifier ordering, lifetime, update timing, and thread interaction.

After trying to fix the crash/deadlock problems locally, it became clear that the resource stack architecture was the root of many of these issues. Fixing one crash often revealed another lifetime or update-order problem. This PR therefore replaces the old 2D skeleton modification system instead of continuing to patch it.

## Additional information

This PR introduces a new 2D skeleton modifier architecture that mirrors the 3D skeleton modifier design more closely.

Main changes:

- Adds `SkeletonModifier2D : Node2D`.
- Adds the 2D IK modifier hierarchy:
  - `IKModifier2D`
  - `ChainIK2D`
  - `IterateIK2D`
  - `CCDIK2D`
  - `FABRIK2D`
  - `TwoBoneIK2D`
- Adds node-based modifiers:
  - `LookAtModifier2D`
  - `JiggleModifier2D`
  - `PhysicalBoneSimulator2D`
- Removes the old resource-based 2D modification system:
  - `SkeletonModificationStack2D`
  - `SkeletonModification2D`
  - `SkeletonModification2DLookAt`
  - `SkeletonModification2DCCDIK`
  - `SkeletonModification2DFABRIK`
  - `SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK`
  - `SkeletonModification2DStackHolder`
  - `SkeletonModification2DJiggle`
  - `SkeletonModification2DPhysicalBones`

The new architecture works as follows:

- `SkeletonModifier2D` nodes must be direct children of `Skeleton2D`.
- `Skeleton2D` caches modifier `ObjectID`s instead of storing a resource stack with a raw skeleton pointer.
- `Skeleton2D` owns runtime bone poses and processes modifiers centrally.
- Modifier processing is deferred through `notify_deferred_thread_group(NOTIFICATION_UPDATE_SKELETON)`.
- `Skeleton2D::advance()` accumulates delta and schedules the deferred update.
- Modifiers write runtime pose through `Skeleton2D::set_bone_pose()` or `Skeleton2D::set_bone_global_pose()`.
- `Skeleton2D` handles modifier influence blending centrally.
- `Bone2D` nodes remain for editing and compatibility, but modifiers no longer directly mutate `Bone2D` node transforms during runtime solving.

This makes 2D skeleton behavior closer to the mature 3D skeleton modifier system and gives `Skeleton2D` a single ownership point for runtime pose updates.

IK math was also updated to avoid relying on the old 2D modification algorithms:

- `TwoBoneIK2D` uses a target node and pole node, matching the 3D two-bone IK workflow conceptually.
- `CCDIK2D`, `FABRIK2D`, `TwoBoneIK2D`, `LookAtModifier2D`, and `JiggleModifier2D` write pose using current skeleton-space bone segment vectors and target vectors.
- Runtime modifiers no longer use `Bone2D::get_bone_angle()` as the source of IK direction.
- `PhysicalBoneSimulator2D` writes through `Skeleton2D::set_bone_global_pose()`, matching the 3D global-pose writeback pattern more closely.

Compatibility notes:

- Existing `AnimationPlayer` and `AnimationTree` animation tracks that animate `Bone2D` transforms should continue to work.
- Existing projects using `SkeletonModificationStack2D` resources will need to recreate their 2D IK/modifier setup using the new node-based modifiers.
- The old resource classes and their documentation are removed.
- `Bone2D` remains available as the editing and compatibility node type.

Areas that may need reviewer attention:

- Editor UX for displaying runtime-modified 2D bone poses. The current runtime pose is owned by `Skeleton2D`, so editor `Bone2D` gizmos may still show the authored/rest node transforms rather than the final modifier result.
- Migration expectations for projects that used the old `SkeletonModificationStack2D` resource API.
- Naming/API consistency with the existing 3D modifier classes.
- Whether additional compatibility stubs or upgrade helpers should be added for old 2D modification resources.

AI disclosure:

AI assistance was used while developing this PR. It was used to help inspect the existing 3D skeleton modifier architecture, compare it with the old 2D skeleton modification system, draft the new 2D class structure, and iterate on C++ implementation details. The code was reviewed and tested locally by the author.
